title: Rating Manual: Cardinal Roadside Assistance Rate Page and Waiting Period
content:
## Rate rule

The full-term premium of a Cardinal Roadside Assistance option, per vehicle, is the six-month premium shown below for a six-month term, and the six-month premium multiplied by 2 for a twelve-month term. The premium is a flat add-on on the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy. It is prorated when the option is added, changed or removed, and unearned option premium is returned on a pro rata basis when the option is removed.

## Rates per vehicle

| Option | Six-month premium | Twelve-month multiplier | Twelve-month premium |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Roadside Basic | $7.80 | 2 | $15.60 |
| Cardinal Roadside Standard | $10.40 | 2 | $20.80 |
| Cardinal Roadside Plus | $14.60 | 2 | $29.20 |
| Cardinal Roadside Plus with Trip Interruption | $19.90 | 2 | $39.80 |
| Cardinal Roadside Premier | $24.80 | 2 | $49.60 |
| Cardinal Roadside Premier RV & Trailer | $34.50 | 2 | $69.00 |

The twelve-month column is the six-month premium multiplied by the twelve-month multiplier of 2.

## Rating notes

- **Per vehicle.** Each option is rated on its own vehicle; a household with options on two vehicles pays each vehicle's option premium.
- **Flat add-on.** The option premium is added to the auto policy premium as a flat amount.
- **Mid-term transactions.** Adding, raising or lowering, and removing the option are each prorated.
- **Return on removal.** Unearned option premium is returned pro rata.

## Waiting period after a new or raised option

A newly added option, or the higher services of a raised option, become available 48 hours after the effective date; a disablement that began before then is not covered. The same 48 hours apply on every option.

Hypothetical illustration (the hour at which the option takes effect is an assumed input): an option takes effect at 9:00 a.m. on a Monday. Its services become available at 9:00 a.m. on the Wednesday.

| Disablement began | Covered by the new option? |
|---|---|
| 8:30 a.m. Wednesday | No: it began before the 48 hours had passed |
| 9:30 a.m. Wednesday | Yes, as far as the waiting period is concerned |

For a raised option, for example from Cardinal Roadside Standard to Cardinal Roadside Plus, the same reasoning applies to the services Cardinal Roadside Plus adds: they are available 48 hours after the raise takes effect.
